violations.title: camelCase import name violates snake_case rule
violations.why: The imported name `applyFilterExpression` uses camelCase. Rule 1.1 requires all functions and variables to use snake_case.
violations.evidence: from utils import slugify, truncate, parse_tags, applyFilterExpression
violations.fix: Rename the function to `apply_filter_expression` in utils.py and update this import.

violations.title: camelCase import name violates snake_case rule
violations.why: The imported name `isAdmin` uses camelCase. Rule 1.1 requires all functions and variables to use snake_case.
violations.evidence: from auth import current_user_id, isAdmin, hash_password, verify_password
violations.fix: Rename the function to `is_admin` in auth.py and update this import.

violations.title: Traceback returned in HTTP response body
violations.why: Rule 4.3 explicitly forbids returning an exception's message or traceback in an HTTP response body. This leaks internal stack frames and implementation details to callers.
violations.fix: Remove the `trace` field from the response. Log the traceback server-side instead (e.g., `app.logger.exception(e)`), and return only a safe error message to the client.

violations.title: Function name uses camelCase instead of snake_case
violations.why: Rule 1.1 requires all functions to use snake_case. `isAdmin` is camelCase.
violations.fix: Rename to `is_admin` and update all call sites.

violations.title: Predicate function not named with is_/has_ snake_case pattern
violations.why: Rule 1.4 requires boolean-returning functions to read as predicates in snake_case form (`is_admin`, `has_access`). `isAdmin` fails both the case requirement (camelCase) and the predicate naming contract.
violations.fix: Rename to `is_admin` (satisfies both rule 1.1 and rule 1.4).

violations.title: Wildcard import from config
violations.why: Rule 2.1 forbids wildcard imports (`from x import *`) because they defeat static analysis and make symbol origins unknowable. This line is pre-existing but is present as context in the diff and the PR author had the opportunity to fix it.
violations.fix: Replace with explicit imports: `from config import DATABASE_URL` (and any other symbols actually used in this module).

violations.title: Function name uses camelCase instead of snake_case
violations.why: Rule 1.1 requires all functions to use snake_case. `insertNote` is camelCase. The function is not new to this PR but is imported on a changed line in app.py, and the PR author had the opportunity to rename it.
violations.fix: Rename to `insert_note` in db.py and update all import and call sites.

violations.title: Mutable default argument `tags=[]` in function signature
violations.why: Rule 3.1 forbids mutable default arguments. The default list object is created once at definition time and shared across all calls that omit the argument, causing state to leak between calls.
violations.fix: Change the signature to `def insertNote(title, body, user_id, tags=None):` and add `if tags is None: tags = []` as the first line of the body.

violations.title: Bare `except:` clause catches all exceptions including BaseException
violations.why: Rule 4.1 forbids bare `except:`. It catches every possible exception, including `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit`, masking serious failures and making debugging impossible.
violations.fix: Catch the narrowest applicable exception, e.g., `except Exception as e:`, and handle or log it appropriately.

violations.title: `except` block contains only `pass` — errors are silently swallowed
violations.why: Rule 4.2 forbids an `except` block that only contains `pass`. If a DELETE fails (e.g., constraint violation, connection error), the failure is completely invisible. The rule requires at minimum a log statement and a comment explaining why the error is ignorable.
violations.fix: At minimum: `except Exception as e: logger.warning("delete_note failed for id=%s: %s", note_id, e)`. If the error is truly ignorable, add a comment explaining why.

violations.title: Function name uses camelCase instead of snake_case
violations.why: Rule 1.1 requires all functions to use snake_case. `applyFilterExpression` is camelCase.
violations.fix: Rename to `apply_filter_expression` and update the import in app.py.
